speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry whether there are measures in place to ensure that entities operating in Singapore are compliant with export controls and international laws in order to protect Singapore’s status as a well-respected international business hub.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These pertain to questions over the United States (US) export controls and Singapore's approach to such measures.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: My response today will also cover a similar Parliamentary Question that has been filed by Mr Mark Lee1, that has been scheduled for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Singapore is a stable, trusted, reliable and well-connected international business hub.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our economic competitiveness is based on our commitment to the rule of law, zero tolerance for corruption, transparent regulations and an open inclusive business environment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have painstakingly built up this reputation over time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That is why we take firm and decisive action against individuals and companies that violate our laws.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Questions have been raised about Nvidia chips that were subject to US export controls.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are mainly deployed in Singapore for major enterprises and the Singapore Government.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We understand that the remainder of Nvidia's revenue billed to business entities in Singapore did not involve physical shipments into Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If a company in Singapore is engaged in deceptive or dishonest practices to evade export controls that it is subject to, we will investigate and we will take the appropriate action in accordance with Singapore laws.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is in our national interest to secure access to leading edge technology and to maintain the integrity of our business environment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Within Singapore, the transfer and brokering of strategic goods and technology is governed by the Strategic Goods (Control) Act.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is a robust framework that is aligned with major multilateral export control regimes, including those imposed by the United Nations Security Council.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Outside of these multilateral regimes, countries sometimes impose unilateral export controls on specific items.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The US' export controls on advanced semi-conductor chips are one example.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Under these rules, the US expects companies to ensure their business transactions adhere to their requirements, including doing the required Know Your Customer (KYC) on the buyers of the advanced semi-conductor chips.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Their international business activities should be conducted transparently.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We certainly do not condone businesses deliberately using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the export controls of other countries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the operational level, Singapore Customs works closely with its foreign counterparts, including those from the US to address their concerns and to facilitate their investigations where appropriate and to the extent our law permits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is important to emphasise that this open, inclusive and transparent regulatory regime applies to all our trading partners.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some Members also had questions about the economic impact on Singapore arising from US controls on advanced semi-conductor chips.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is limited impact, in terms of our ability to manufacture and export chips.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, in terms of access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) compute – for example Nvidia H100 Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), the previous US administration had introduced an AI Diffusion Rule in January 2025 aimed at managing access to H100 or equivalent GPUs on a country-level basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The details of the US AI Diffusion Rule have not yet been finalised by the current US administration, and the US has not communicated any specific requirements as prerequisites for changes to countries' tiering classifications.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our objective is to ensure adequate access to AI compute by both local and international companies with operations in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will ensure that US-headquartered cloud hyperscalers can continue to operate in Singapore as Universal Verified End Users and also support local companies that wish to apply to be National Verified End Users with access to AI compute.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In closing, I wish to assure Members that we will continue to work with companies based in Singapore to facilitate their access to advanced semi-conductor chips and technologies from all the major source countries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will also continue to engage the US administration to address their concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I declare that I work in a global investment firm based in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am glad that the Ministry has emphasised compliance with international trade rules, and that Singapore takes our obligations seriously.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Minister elaborate on the safeguards in place, to prevent companies from using Singapore as a conduit to bypass US export restrictions, especially in light of heightened US-China trade tensions?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And how does the Ministry balance these safeguards with ensuring that we remain an attractable destination for businesses?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Singapore has a robust export control regime and this is underpinned by a comprehensive strategic goods control legislation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And as I have alluded to earlier, the enforcement action is undertaken by Singapore Customs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I wanted to give a bit more granularity in terms of how we manage the exports.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Potential contraventions can include export, transshipment, transit of strategic goods without the requisite permits or providing false or misleading documents or information, incorrect declarations and brokering of strategic goods without a permit or being registered – and with that, criminal penalties can then be enforced.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: How do we balance working with foreign counterparts?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have earlier on mentioned in my reply, while we may currently not have legal obligations to enforce unilateral export controls of other countries, which may vary from time to time, companies that are operating in Singapore are expected to take into account such regulations if these apply to their international business activities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) and Singapore Customs also have existing arrangements with some foreign counterparts, such as those in the US, to facilitate the investigation of companies of interest.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From time to time, when we do get information of allegations and if we are aware of breaches, we will undertake to conduct these investigations ourselves.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The approach that we take is systematic and thorough, and we want to continue to emphasise that we have an open, inclusive and transparent regulatory regime and it applies to all of our partners today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that addresses Mr Yip's supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on, countries may have export controls from time to time, unilaterally.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Where we have been very clear and transparent to companies operating within Singapore is that they are expected to abide by the countries' export controls, and not use Singapore as a country to bypass or circumvent these export controls.
To this end, as the hon Member has highlighted, it would not be possible to cover every potential, probable or future export controls that countries may unilaterally impose.
But those principles that have guided us through to build us up to where we are a reputable business hub, these principles will continue to be consistent and we will hold true to these principles.

From time to time, when these unilateral export controls come to our attention, we will work with the relevant countries to gain clarity, to engage them, as we are actively engaging with the US, our very important partner, to see how we can better manage and better educate the businesses that are based here to make sure that they are able to comply.
I hope that gives the Member the reassurance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand the motivation behind this redirection, but hopeful that the Minister or a Minister from MFA will be able to respond to questions that call for a more foreign policy approach.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The next highest source is actually Singapore, with around $7 billion, and it is more than that for China, which includes Hong Kong, at $12 billion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This means that Singapore accounts for around 20% of Nvidia's global revenue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It is not unusual for entrepôt hubs like us to book such inflated revenue figures, even if our value-added component is small or negligible, nor is this really about fraud, as the Minister seems to allude to, but actually legitimate accounting practices and rules of origin machinations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Regardless, the headline imbalance invites commercial action, like what we have seen.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, if I may enquire if MFA was aware of these imbalances and if so, is it, in its assessment, that facilitating transshipment trade is positive or negative for the national interest from a foreign policy angle?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our trade volume is three times our gross domestic product (GDP), and the range of activities that our companies are engaged in, and not just companies owned by Singapore and Singaporeans, but by global owners of these companies, have a regional and international footprint.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, I am not sure what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is referring to when he says imbalances.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, there is nothing unusual or unbalanced about that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The nub of the question really is whether Singapore is being used by these enterprises and companies to evade unilateral export controls.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And my colleague has very carefully explained to this House that Singapore, by law, through the Strategic Goods Control Act, gives effect to multilateral export control regimes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He referred to the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group and the Missile Technology Control Regime.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Basically, these are focused especially on weapons or weapons of mass destruction, chemical and biological threats, and other potentially significant dual-use equipment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And these have force of law and we take our reference from the United Nations Security Council.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The point is the onus is on that company and we will not countenance evasion, deception, false declarations or even mis-accounting; and that we will act on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And as and when a trading partner comes to us and says, "We have concerns", at that point, we would certainly facilitate investigations or at least, have a deeper look at the data and see whether there is any cause for concern, and we do that in order to protect our own national interest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is true that we are also part of the global chains that manufacture and export semi-conductors.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But those that are currently manufactured in Singapore are not the H100s, the high-end chips which are used for AI.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we need them for our own purposes and we therefore have to monitor the export regimes of the manufacturers of these chips.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Member referred to our Tier Two classification.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Well, first of all, they call it the AI Diffusion Rule.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It was first published near the tail-end of the Biden Administration.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, right now, the rules are up for comments and the situation is still evolving.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are not in Tier One, but we are in Tier Two, in good company with about 150 other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I do not want to get into detail about the exact number of chips and whether that currently poses a constraint for us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Needless to say, we will continue to engage the major exporting source of these advanced chips to ensure that we have adequate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I am sure Members of this House will also be aware, when dealing with sensitive topics like this, it is not in our national interest to compromise our negotiating positions when it deals with strategic items on this score.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, I hope the Member understands that the situation that has arisen is: one, because of our unique role and indeed our successful performance of this unique, global role; and two, the fact that we are a trusted, reliable and honest player.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you zoom out, beyond chips and export controls, the point is this: Singapore, as a tiny island city-state and a trading hub, we do need to stand in favour of free trade.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do need to play a critical role in global supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second point, because we are small, we have to subscribe to international law and multilateral rules, and processes and institutions to give effect to multilateral rules.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third point, we always have to seek to be relevant to the world, to be useful to big and middle powers, but we will not be made use of, either by other powers or even by companies pursuing pecuniary interest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And my final point, in a world which is bifurcating, fracturing or polarising and divided, it is all the more important for us to play it straight, for me to say the same thing in Beijing and Washington, and to be fair.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And that is why everything that Minister Tan has said applies to all our trading partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I hope I have reassured the Member and other Members of this House.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This reflects the location where Nvidia's customers received the bill; it does not mean that it was shipped here.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is independent from the physical location that Nvidia and its customers deliver the goods to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The remainder of Nvidia's revenue billed to business entities here did not involve physical shipments into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister has mentioned that Singapore has been classified as a Tier Two country under the US AI chip export controls.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: My supplementary question to the Minister is: what are the economic implications of being in Tier Two and does this classification impact Singapore's ability to attract AI chip investments, high-end semi-conductor research and development or even hinder our ambitions to be an AI development hub?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As my esteemed colleague, Minister Vivian, has shared, we are in the broader base of the 150 countries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have also mentioned in my reply earlier, the US AI Diffusion Rule has not yet been finalised by the current administration; and Minister Vivian has also alluded to the fact that it was released by the Biden Administration in the final days of his administration.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And there is a 120-day comment period, which will end on 13 May 2025.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The new administration has not commented on their policy or position towards the rule.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we are among one of the 150 countries under this Tier Two status.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Whilst the US categorised 18 countries under Tier One, it did not share specific requirements on the tiering classification nor what requirements are required for a country to be reclassified from Tier Two to Tier One.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Access to AI compute is important for our national AI ambitions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As articulated in our National AI Strategy 2.0, we are adopting a multi-prong strategy to enable industry, academia and Government to undertake high-value AI activities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Besides securing access to advanced AI hardware and compute, we will also focus on talent and infrastructure development.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will continue to support companies operating in Singapore to gain access to advanced chips, including those that are under the AI Diffusion Rule.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Presently, most of the demand for advanced chips amongst our industry players come from US headquartered cloud hyperscalers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are: Meta, Amazon, Google and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will work with them to apply to be universal verified end users, so as to allow them to transfer a certain quantity of advanced chips to Singapore for their innovation and for their business needs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the local companies with significant AI compute requirements, they can apply to be the national verified end user.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are two tiers: a universal verified end user and a national verified end user.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They can apply for the national verified end user status to receive access to advanced AI chips and we will support our local companies in their application.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are in consultation with industry players in Singapore to gather feedback on the potential impact of the draft rules on their business activities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This will allow us to better consider appropriate measures to support our companies and we are also, as I have said earlier, engaging the US to address their concerns and to also better understand their approach to the AI Diffusion Rule.
